title: Capacity, slack, and the illusion of a team allocated at 100%

videos.script: Here is a spreadsheet every large company has. Names down the side, projects across the top, and every row adds up to exactly one hundred per cent. {{sheet}} It looks efficient. Nobody is idle. {{efficient}} It is a picture of the most expensive place a team can be. {{expensive}} Watch one person get busier. At half busy, a request waits about a day. At ninety-five per cent, it waits nearly three weeks, for one day of work. {{curve}} That curve is why the Billing team's reviews took seven days in July. One person did them all, and she was full. {{bia}} This lesson draws the curve on your computer. Then it works out how much of a team's week is really free for planned work. {{capacity}} And it makes the case for slack: room left on purpose, so the team can answer when something arrives. {{slack}}
